scene.label: 3D view of the solar system
scene.title: View of the mission
scene.noWebgl: This browser cannot show the 3D view because WebGL 2 is not available. All other functions of the application operate.
scene.lost: The browser stopped the 3D view and removed its memory.
scene.scaleNote: All bodies and the spacecraft have their actual size and their actual distance. A point, a diamond, a ring, a name and a line have a constant size on the screen. They show a position, not a size.
scene.attitudeNote: The attitude of the spacecraft is an example: the antenna points to the Earth. The trajectory calculation does not use the attitude.
scene.perspectiveNote: In a view from near the spacecraft, the flight path can show an angle. The angle is an effect of the perspective. It is at the point where the path and the line from the camera have the same direction. The path is a curve with no angle.
scene.sunlightNote: The sunlight has the same brightness at all distances from the Sun. With the actual brightness, the outer planets are too dark on a screen.
scene.nightNote: The night side of a body gets a small quantity of light that is not physical. Without this light, the night side is black. The 3D view of the Expert mode has a control that sets this light to off.
scene.effectsNote: The motion of the clouds and of the surface of the Sun is a display effect, not data. It stops when the time stops.
scene.pathSsb: Flight path: relative to the solar system barycenter.
scene.howTo: Turn the view: move one finger, or move the mouse with the button down. Change the distance: use two fingers or the mouse wheel.
scene.toStart: Go to the start of the flight
scene.toEnd: Go to the end of the flight
scene.prevEvent: Go to the event before this time
scene.timeline: Time of the view in the flight
